name: Anterior approach to the radial shaft (Henry)
corridor: Between brachioradialis laterally and flexor carpi radialis medially, with level-specific deep elevation of supinator, pronator teres, flexor pollicis longus, and pronator quadratus

positioning.text: Position supine with the arm on a radiolucent hand table and the forearm freely rotatable through pronation and supination.

setup.text: Prepare the entire limb, verify the required proximal-to-distal exposure and plate trajectory, and preserve access for fluoroscopy and forearm rotation.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the biceps tendon proximally, the palpable medial border of brachioradialis, the radial styloid distally, and the projected radial shaft.

incision.text: Place a longitudinal incision along the line from the biceps tendon to the radial styloid, limiting its length to the radial segment requiring exposure.

superficial_interval.text: Develop the interval between brachioradialis laterally and flexor carpi radialis medially; identify the radial artery and its venae comitantes and protect the superficial radial nerve beneath brachioradialis.

deep_interval.text: For proximal exposure, fully supinate and elevate supinator from its medial edge; for the middle third, pronate to address the pronator-teres insertion; distally, elevate flexor pollicis longus and pronator quadratus as required.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, forearm fascia, brachioradialis–flexor carpi radialis interval, radial neurovascular plane, level-specific deep muscle, periosteum, then radius.

structures_encountered.text: Brachioradialis, flexor carpi radialis, radial artery with venae comitantes, superficial radial nerve, supinator, pronator teres, flexor pollicis longus, and pronator quadratus are encountered according to level.

structures_at_risk.text: The posterior interosseous nerve proximally, superficial radial nerve, radial artery and branches, palmar cutaneous branch of the median nerve distally, and pronator/supinator insertions are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The posterior interosseous nerve runs within supinator; full supination moves it away from the proximal anterior field, and supinator elevation must remain limited and subperiosteal.

retraction_hazards.text: Retract the superficial radial nerve laterally and radial artery medially without sustained focal pressure; control lateral arterial branches before mobilization rather than avulsing them.

exposure.text: The extensile anterior corridor can expose the full radial shaft, with the operative segment selected by incision length and level-specific deep dissection.

limitations.text: Proximal exposure places the posterior interosseous nerve at risk, and the deep muscular interval changes by radial level; distal-only work may be better served by a modified Henry corridor.

extensions.text: Extend longitudinally toward the biceps tendon or radial styloid while preserving the same superficial interval and changing the deep release only at the required radial level.

indications.text: Use for fixation or reconstruction requiring anterior access to the proximal, middle, distal, or multiple levels of the radial shaft.

relative_contraindications.text: Choose an alternative corridor when compromised volar soft tissue, prior scarring, vascular concerns, or the required dorsal target makes anterior dissection less safe.

implant_implications.text: Seat implants directly on bone without interposed soft tissue and document the posterior interosseous nerve's relationship to a proximal plate if the nerve is exposed.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Obtain orthogonal views to confirm reduction, radial bow, plate position, screw length, and proximal and distal radioulnar-joint alignment.

closure.text: Repair elevated pronator quadratus when feasible, confirm neurovascular structures are free, obtain hemostasis, and use a tension-free skin closure; defer closure when swelling makes it unsafe.

complications.text: Complications include posterior interosseous or superficial radial neuropathy, radial-artery injury, compartment syndrome, wound problems, tendon adhesion, infection, synostosis, malunion, and nonunion.

bailouts.text: If proximal nerve safety or a level-specific deep interval cannot be established, stop blind elevation, enlarge the exposure for identification, or use a separate appropriate corridor rather than force retraction.

procedure_applications.condition: Direct anterior exposure of the proximal, middle, or distal radial shaft is required
The radius is exposed through a separate anterior incision and the ulna through a separate ulnar approach

questions.question: What is the superficial Henry interval?
questions.answer: Brachioradialis laterally and flexor carpi radialis medially.

questions.question: How is the forearm positioned for proximal supinator elevation?
questions.answer: Fully supinated to move the posterior interosseous nerve away from the field.

questions.question: Where is the superficial radial nerve in the approach?
questions.answer: Beneath brachioradialis, lateral to the radial artery.
